facts.statement: Stokesosaurus were small, bipedal predators measuring approximately 3 to 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: They were small, bipedal predators measuring around 3 to 4 m in length.

facts.statement: The type species Stokesosaurus clevelandi was named and described by James Henry Madsen in 1974.
facts.quote: In 1974 Madsen named and described the type species Stokesosaurus clevelandi.

facts.statement: The generic name Stokesosaurus honors the geologist William Lee Stokes.
facts.quote: Its generic name honours Stokes.

facts.statement: The specific name clevelandi refers to the town of Cleveland, Utah.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the town of Cleveland, Utah.

facts.statement: The holotype of Stokesosaurus, a left ilium from a juvenile, was found in the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation and dates to about 150 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype (UMNH 2938, also known as UMNH VP 7473 and formerly known as UUVP 2938) was uncovered in the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation dating from the early Tithonian stage, about 150 million years old.

facts.statement: The holotype ilium measures 22 cm in length, indicating that the individual was small.
facts.quote: The holotype ilium is 22 cm long, indicating a small individual.

facts.statement: In 1974, Madsen estimated the adult body length of Stokesosaurus to be about 4 meters.
facts.quote: Madsen in 1974 estimated that the adult body length was about 4 m.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Stokesosaurus at 2.5 meters and the weight at 60 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 2.5 m and the weight at 60 kg.

facts.statement: Stokesosaurus was a small predator ranging between 2 and 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Stokesosaurus fue un pequeño depredador de entre 2 y 5 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Like primitive tyrannosauroids, Stokesosaurus had a small head, a light build, and long arms.
facts.quote: Como los primitivos tiranosauroideos, poseía una cabeza pequeña, una constitución ligera y largos brazos.

facts.statement: Fragmentary remains possibly belonging to Stokesosaurus have been found in the Morrison Formation dating to about 152 million years ago.
facts.quote: More fragmentary remains possibly referable to Stokesosaurus have been recovered from stratigraphic zone 2 of the Morrison Formation, dated to the late Kimmeridgian age, about 152 million years ago.

facts.statement: The Morrison Formation, where Stokesosaurus fossils were found, spans from 156.3 to 146.8 million years ago, covering the late Oxfordian, Kimmeridgian, and early Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: The Morrison Formation is a sequence of shallow marine and alluvial sediments which, according to radiometric dating, ranges between 156.3 million years old (Ma) at its base, to 146.8 million years old at the top, which places it in the late Oxfordian, Kimmeridgian, and early Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic period.

facts.statement: The Morrison Formation environment is interpreted as semiarid with distinct wet and dry seasons.
facts.quote: This formation is interpreted as a semiarid environment with distinct wet and dry seasons.

facts.statement: Stokesosaurus lived alongside gigantic sauropods including Camarasaurus, Barosaurus, Diplodocus, Apatosaurus, and Brachiosaurus.
facts.quote: The Morrison Formation records an environment and time dominated by gigantic sauropod dinosaurs such as Camarasaurus, Barosaurus, Diplodocus, Apatosaurus and Brachiosaurus.

facts.statement: Stokesosaurus shared its environment with apex predators like Allosaurus, which made up 70 to 75% of theropod specimens in the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: Predators in this paleoenvironment included the theropods Saurophaganax, Torvosaurus, Ceratosaurus, Marshosaurus, Ornitholestes and Allosaurus, which accounted for 70 to 75% of theropod specimens and was at the top trophic level of the Morrison food web.

facts.statement: A 2012 study classified Stokesosaurus as a basal member of the Tyrannosauroidea, closely related to Eotyrannus and Juratyrant.
facts.quote: In 2012 the study by Brusatte and Benson recovered Stokesosaurus as a basal member of the Tyrannosauroidea, and closely related to Eotyrannus and Juratyrant.

facts.statement: A 2013 analysis placed Stokesosaurus and Juratyrant as derived members of Proceratosauridae based on a shared narrow preacetabular notch.
facts.quote: Below is a 2013 cladogram by Loewen et al. that places Stokesosaurus and Juratyrant as derived members of Proceratosauridae, due to sharing with Sinotyrannus a narrow preacetabular notch.

facts.statement: Stokesosaurus is classified within the superfamily Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Tyrannosauroidea

facts.statement: Stokesosaurus is classified within the family Stokesosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Stokesosauridae

facts.statement: It is debated whether Stokesosaurus is a synonym of Iliosuchus, a hypothesis proposed by Galton in 1976 that he later withdrew in 1980 and which was not accepted by other researchers.
facts.quote: In 1976 Peter Malcolm Galton considered Stokesosaurus to be a second species of the British possible early tyrannosauroid Iliosuchus, that he named as Iliosuchus clevelandi. This has found no acceptance among other researchers; in 1980 Galton himself withdrew his opinion.

facts.statement: Benson and Brusatte debated that no bones other than the holotype ilium could be safely assigned to Stokesosaurus.
facts.quote: Benson and Stephen Brusatte concluded that not a single bone had been justifiably referred to Stokesosaurus, and that not even the paratype could be safely assigned, leaving the holotype ilium as the only known fossil of the taxon.

facts.statement: A trait once thought unique to Stokesosaurus, a posterodorsally inclined ridge on the ilium, was also found on the holotype of Eotyrannus.
facts.quote: In fact, one of the traits, a posterodorsally inclined ridge on the lateral side of the ilium, was found on the undescribed left ilium of the holotype of Eotyrannus.

facts.statement: Stokesosaurus clevelandi was named and described by James Henry Madsen in 1974.
facts.quote: En 1974 Madsen nombró y describió la especie tipo Stokesosaurus clevelandi.

facts.statement: The specific name clevelandi refers to the city of Cleveland, Utah.
facts.quote: El nombre específico se refiere a la ciudad de Cleveland, Utah.

facts.statement: The holotype, a left ilium from a juvenile individual, was discovered in the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation dating to the early Tithonian stage, approximately 150 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo, UMNH 293, también conocido como UMNH VP 7473 y anteriormente conocido como UUVP 2938 fue descubierto en el Miembro de la Cuenca Brushy de la Formación Morrison que data de la etapa Titoniense temprana, de unos 150 millones de años.

facts.statement: Madsen assigned a right ilium paratype, UUVP 2320, which is 50% larger than the holotype.
facts.quote: Madsen también asignó un paratipo , UUVP 2320, un ilion derecho un 50% más grande.

facts.statement: In 1976, Peter Malcolm Galton considered Stokesosaurus to be a second species of the British tyrannosauroid Iliosuchus, naming it Iliosuchus clevelandi.
facts.quote: En 1976 , Peter Malcolm Galton consideró a Stokesosaurus como una segunda especie del posible tiranosaurioide primitivo británico Iliosuchus, al que denominó Iliosuchus clevelandi.

facts.statement: The ilium of Tanycolagreus, the best-known part of that taxon, was never discovered, making comparison with Stokesosaurus difficult.
facts.quote: Sin embargo el ilion, la parte mejor conocida de Stokesosaurus, de Tanycolagreus nunca fue descubierto, lo que dificulta la comparación.

facts.statement: A second species, Stokesosaurus langhami, was described by Roger Benson in 2008 based on a partial skeleton found in England.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, Stokesosaurus langhami, descrita por Roger Benson en 2008, basado en un esqueleto pascial encontrado en Inglaterra.

facts.statement: A later study showed that Stokesosaurus langhami should be referred to a new genus named Juratyrant in 2012.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un estudio posterior mostró que esta especie debería ser referida a un nuevo género, que fue nombrado Juratyrant en 2012.

facts.statement: Benson and Stephen Brusatte concluded that no bones were justifiably referred to Stokesosaurus except the holotype ilium, as the paratype could not be assigned with certainty.
facts.quote: Benson y Stephen Brusatte concluyeron que ni un solo hueso había sido referido justificadamente a Stokesosaurus , y que ni siquiera el paratipo podría ser asignado con seguridad, dejando el holotipo ilion como el único fósil conocido del taxón.

facts.statement: In 1974, Madsen assigned Stokesosaurus to the family Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: En 1974 Madsen asignó Stokesosaurus a la familia Tyrannosauridae.

facts.statement: Modern cladistic analyses indicate that Stokesosaurus holds a more basal position than originally thought.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los modernos análisis cladísticos indican una posición más basal.

facts.statement: A 2012 study by Brusatte and Benson found that Stokesosaurus was a basal member of Tyrannosauroidea, closely related to Eotyrannus and Juratyrant.
facts.quote: En 2012 el estudio publicado por Brusatte y Benson encontró que Stokesosaurus era un miembro basal de Tyrannosauroidea, y emparentado de cerca con Eotyrannus y Juratyrant.

facts.statement: In 2013, Loewen et al. placed Stokesosaurus and Juratyrant as derived members of Proceratosauridae because they share a narrow preacetabular notch with Sinotyrannus.
facts.quote: En 2013 de Loewen et al. que ubica a Stokesosaurus y Juratyrant como miembros derivados de Proceratosauridae, debido a que comparten con Sinotyrannus una estrecha muesca preacetabular.

facts.statement: In parsimonious phylogenies, Eotyrannus is recovered as a sister taxon to Stokesosaurus and Juratyrant.
facts.quote: Además, Eotyrannus se recupera como un taxón hermano de estos géneros en la filogenia parsimoniosa.

facts.statement: Fragmentary remains possibly attributable to Stokesosaurus date to the late Kimmeridgian, approximately 152 million years ago.
facts.quote: Se han recuperado más restos fragmentarios posiblemente atribuibles a Stokesosaurus de la zona estratigráfica 2 de la Formación Morrison, que datan de finales del Kimmeridgiano, hace unos 152 millones de años.

facts.statement: Stokesosaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 154.8 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Morrison Formation, where Stokesosaurus fossils were found, dates from the late Oxfordian to early Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic, between 156.3 and 146.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: La Formación Morrison es una secuencia de sedimentos marinos y aluviales someros que, según dataciones radiométricas, oscila entre 156,3 millones de años en su base, a 146,8 millones de años en la parte superior, lo que la sitúa en las etapas del Oxfordiense tardío, Kimmeridgiense y Titoniense temprano del período Jurásico tardío.

facts.statement: The Morrison Formation is interpreted as a semi-arid environment with distinct wet and dry seasons.
facts.quote: Esta formación se interpreta como un ambiente semiárido con estaciones húmedas y secas diferenciadas.

facts.statement: The Morrison Basin, where dinosaurs lived, extended from New Mexico to Alberta and Saskatchewan.
facts.quote: La cuenca de Morrison, donde vivían los dinosaurios, se extendía desde Nuevo México hasta Alberta y Saskatchewan

Consiste en un ilion izquierdo o hueso de la cadera, perteneciente a un individuo juvenil.

facts.statement: A right premaxilla was originally referred to Stokesosaurus but was reassigned to Tanycolagreus in 2005.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente refirió un premaxilar derecho , UUVP 2999. Sin embargo, esto fue en 2005 referido a Tanycolagreus .

facts.statement: Later findings referred to Stokesosaurus included some ischia and tail vertebrae found in 1991 and a partial skull found in 1998.
facts.quote: Algunos hallazgos posteriores fueron referidos a Stokesosaurus. Esto incluyó algunos isquiones y vértebras de la cola en 1991 y un cráneo parcial en 1998.

facts.statement: A posterodorsally inclined crest on the lateral side of the ilium, a trait linking Stokesosaurus and Juratyrant, was also found in the undescribed left ilium of the Eotyrannus holotype.
facts.quote: Uno de los rasgos, una cresta inclinada posterodorsalmente en el lado lateral del ilion, se encontró en el ilion izquierdo no descrito del holotipo de Eotyrannus.

facts.statement: Stokesosaurus has only one unique autapomorphy not present in Juratyrant or other tyrannosauroids: a swollen rim around the articular surface of the pubic peduncle.
facts.quote: Esto deja solo una única autapomorfia de Stokesosaurus que no está presente en Juratyrant u otros tiranosauroides, un borde hinchado alrededor de la superficie articular del pedúnculo púbico.

facts.statement: An ilium once referred to Stokesosaurus is now considered part of Aviatyrannis, and a premaxilla thought to belong to Iliosuchus is now part of Tanycolagreus.
facts.quote: Otro ilion referido a este dinosaurio se ha perdido, pero actualmente se lo considera parte de un Aviatyrannis, y el premaxilar se creyó que perteneció a Iliosuchus es actualmente parte de Tanycolagreus.

facts.statement: A very small ilium found in South Dakota and referred to Stokesosaurus may actually belong to Aviatyrannis, a close relative.
facts.quote: Otro ilion muy pequeño referido a Stokesosaurus, encontrado en Dakota del Sur, se ha perdido pero en realidad puede pertenecer a Aviatyrannis, un pariente cercano.

facts.quote: Sin embargo, un estudio posterior mostró que esta especie debería ser referida a un nuevo género, que fue nombrado Juratyrant en 2012. Benson y Stephen Brusatte concluyeron que ni un solo hueso había sido referido justificadamente a Stokesosaurus , y que ni siquiera el paratipo podría ser asignado con seguridad, dejando el holotipo ilion como el único fósil conocido del taxón.

facts.statement: In 2013, Loewen et al. proposed that Stokesosaurus and Juratyrant are derived members of Proceratosauridae based on a shared preacetabular notch with Sinotyrannus.
facts.quote: En 2013 de Loewen et al. que ubica a Stokesosaurus y Juratyrant como miembros derivados de Proceratosauridae, debido a que comparten con Sinotyrannus una estrecha muesca preacetabular.
